key_insight: Real-space electronic obstruction in topological insulators can strongly amplify and even sign-control the shift current, enabling larger bulk photovoltaic response without major changes to the band structure.
engineering_relevance: This points to a materials-design route for infrared photovoltaic and optoelectronic devices by targeting non-centrosymmetric, low-gap quantum spin Hall systems with obstructed Wannier centers.
method: Built a tight-binding model of a triangular-lattice quantum spin Hall insulator.
Compared nonlinear photocurrent across trivial, quantum spin Hall, and higher-order topological phases.
Analyzed optical transitions between distinct Wannier-center sectors to explain shift-current enhancement.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a substantially enhanced shift-current response in obstructed topological phases, with the sign controlled by the topological phase, and identifies indenene as a promising candidate material.
watch_item: The result is model-based, so experimental verification is still needed to confirm the predicted shift-current magnitude and sign in real materials.
paper_title: Real-space obstruction control of the shift current in two-dimensional Quantum Spin Hall insulators
